articles.title: 'A number of players playing for their careers': Simon Katich blasts batting approach as Australia fight to save 2nd Test
articles.summary: Australia are under pressure in the second Test against South Africa, with former batter Simon Katich warning that several players could be fighting to
articles.body: Australia are under pressure in the second Test against South Africa, with former batter Simon Katich warning that several players could be fighting to save their places in the team. Marnus Labuschagne, Nic Maddinson and Beau Webster have struggled in the match, leaving Australia with plenty to prove on the final day in Gqeberha.Australia were 156/4 at the end of Day 4 after being asked to follow on, still trailing South Africa by 170 runs. Labuschagne scored 39 before throwing away his wicket with an attacking shot against spinner Simon Harmer. Despite getting starts in recent matches, the batter has struggled to convert them into big scores.Katich questioned Labuschagne’s decision to play an aggressive shot when Australia were trying to save the match. "There are a number of players playing for their careers in this innings," Katich said on SEN radio.He added, "Only he knows what was going through his mind when he tried to take Harmer down the ground, against the breeze, when Australia are trying to play for a draw."Katich also questioned how selectors would view the dismissal, pointing out that Labuschagne had received several opportunities over the years.Labuschagne under pressure as Australia fight backAustralia head coach Andrew McDonald was also disappointed with Labuschagne’s latest failure. The 32-year-old has not scored a Test century since July 2023 and continues to struggle to turn promising starts into substantial innings."I feel like I am on repeat" McDonald said, reflecting on Labuschagne’s repeated scores in the 30s.He added that Australia had built a useful partnership and were beginning to recover before Labuschagne’s dismissal. "When you do that hard work, you've got to cash in, and unfortunately, that wasn't to be the case for Marn. We were disappointed, and he will be too," the coach said.South Africa close in as pressure mountsAustralia lead the three-match series 1-0 after winning the first Test at Kingsmead by 214 runs. However, South Africa have fought back strongly in Gqeberha, declaring at 425/9 before dismissing Australia for just 99 in their first innings.Rain limited play during the first two days, but South Africa have put themselves in a strong position to win the match. Travis Head, unbeaten on 87, and nightwatchman Scott Boland will resume Australia's innings on the final day.Australia's team management could face further scrutiny if the visitors lose, particularly after Nathan Lyon's omission from the playing XI drew criticism.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt handed two-match ban for medication breach
articles.summary: Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt has been handed a two-match suspension for failing to comply with requirements governing the use of prescription
articles.body: Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt has been handed a two-match suspension for failing to comply with requirements governing the use of prescription medication, Cricket Australia (CA) said on Thursday.The 33-year-old will miss Australia's third and final T20I against New Zealand at North Sydney Oval on Thursday, as well as Adelaide Strikers' opening match of the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) against Melbourne Stars on October 31.Cricket Australia clarified that the breach involved a single incident that occurred outside competition and was not related to performance enhancement. The suspension applies to both international and domestic cricket.Cricket Australia clarifies nature of breachIn a statement, CA said the offence involved non-compliance with its medical guidelines governing prescription medication."The breach was a failure to adhere to requirements under the Sports Science and Sports Medicine guidelines with regard to prescription medication," Cricket Australia said.The governing body also stressed that the incident was isolated and had occurred outside the competitive environment."This (breach) relates to a single incidence which occurred while out of competition and was not for performance enhancing purposes," CA added.The suspension means Schutt will be unavailable for Australia's series-deciding T20I against New Zealand and will also miss the beginning of her domestic campaign with Adelaide Strikers.Schutt accepts sanction and apologisesSchutt accepted the suspension and apologised for not meeting the standards expected of players representing Australian cricket."I fully accept the penalty handed down and apologise for failing to meet the standards expected of me. I'm sorry for the attention this has caused and appreciate the support I've received," Schutt said in her statement.The fast bowler acknowledged that players were regularly educated about the relevant guidelines and accepted responsibility for complying with them."While this occurred out of competition and was not performance related, I understand that I am responsible for following the Sports Science and Sports Medicine Guidelines, which players receive regular education on, and I should have adhered to these guidelines," she added.CA said it would continue to provide appropriate support to Schutt while reinforcing the standards and responsibilities expected of everyone representing the game.Suspension follows impressive ODI seriesThe ban comes after Schutt enjoyed an outstanding ODI series against Bangladesh, finishing as Player of the Series after taking 10 wickets at an average of 7.1.Her absence is a setback for Australia ahead of the final T20I against New Zealand, while Adelaide Strikers will also have to manage without the experienced pacer for their WBBL opener.The suspension is limited to two matches, with CA's statement making clear that the incident was not related to performance-enhancing purposes.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: First time in history! India bowlers make unwanted record as New Zealand run riot
articles.summary: For the first time in men’s T20I cricket, five Indian bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in an innings as New Zealand piled up 225/8 in the first T20I in
articles.body: For the first time in men’s T20I cricket, five Indian bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in an innings as New Zealand piled up 225/8 in the first T20I in Christchurch on Thursday. The hosts took advantage of India's struggles with the ball, with Finn Allen scoring 45 off 24 balls and Glenn Phillips remaining unbeaten on 82 off 40.The feat had occurred 13 times overall in men’s T20Is, but this was the first instance involving five Indian bowlers in the same innings. Bhuvneshwar Kumar conceded 49 runs in four overs, Arshdeep Singh gave away 45, Mayank Yadav 40, Axar Patel 51 and Nitish Reddy 40.New Zealand's total was the joint-highest against India in T20Is and their highest on home soil.With Jasprit Bumrah not part of the squad, the Indian attack struggled to contain the hosts despite some early swing on offer. New Zealand's openers dealt with the movement before taking on the bowlers, with Tim Seifert scoring 24 off 17 balls.Bhuvneshwar, playing his first international match in nearly four years, began with a decent first over. However, Seifert hit him for two fours and a six over long-on in his next over, which cost India 17 runs.Allen then attacked Arshdeep in the following over, which also went for 17 runs, giving New Zealand momentum in the powerplay. The openers were particularly effective at finding boundaries on the off-side.Mayank was brought into the attack during the powerplay and gave India a breakthrough when Seifert was caught behind off the final ball of the fifth over.Axar was handed the final over of the powerplay, but the left-arm spinner conceded two sixes. Allen cleared long-off before Daryl Mitchell stepped out and sent the ball over the long-on boundary. New Zealand reached 65/1 in the first six overs.Arshdeep dismissed Mitchell in his second spell, but Bhuvneshwar continued to struggle. His third over cost 14 runs before he was given the responsibility of bowling the final over, which also went for 14. He finished with figures of 0/49 in four overs.Phillips remained unbeaten and finished the innings with a switch hit over cover. Bevon Jacobs also made an impact with 31 off 16 balls, including a first-ball six down the ground off Arshdeep.New Zealand scored 67 runs in the final five overs to cross the 200-run mark, putting India's bowling attack under pressure throughout the innings.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Abhishek Sharma scripts history, sets unique six-hitting record in New Zealand T20I
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma set a new record for hitting the first ball he faced for a six most often in T20Is, but India had a huge target to chase after New Zealand
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma set a new record for hitting the first ball he faced for a six most often in T20Is, but India had a huge target to chase after New Zealand posted 225/8 in the opening T20I in Christchurch on Thursday.Chasing 226, Abhishek faced his first delivery off the final ball of the first over and sent Matt Henry over the cover boundary for a six. Henry bowled a full delivery wide of off stump, but Abhishek went through with his lofted drive and cleared the ropes to reach the milestone.Abhishek has now hit the first ball he faced for a six seven times in T20Is, moving ahead of Afghanistan's Shafiqullah Shinwari, who has done so six times. Suryakumar Yadav is third on the list with five such sixes, while Ireland's Paul Stirling, New Zealand's Colin Munro and the UAE's Mohammad Naveed have managed it four times each.Most sixes off the first ball faced in T20Is7 — Abhishek Sharma (India)6 — Shafiqullah Shinwari (Afghanistan)5 — Suryakumar Yadav (India)4 — Paul Stirling (Ireland)4 — Colin Munro (New Zealand)4 — Mohammad Naveed (UAE)Abhishek and Sanju Samson gave India the quick start they needed, putting together 93 runs for the opening wicket in just 5.5 overs. However, Michael Bracewell ended the partnership by dismissing Abhishek for 29 off 12 balls. The left-hander struck three sixes and two fours during his brief innings.The partnership also saw Abhishek and Samson equal the record for the most 50-plus opening stands by an Indian pair in T20Is in a calendar year. Their stand was their fifth such partnership in 2026, putting them alongside two other Indian pairs on the list.Most 50-plus opening stands for India in a calendar year in T20Is5 — KL Rahul and Rohit Sharma (2021)5 — Abhishek Sharma and Shubman Gill (2025)5 — Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson (2026)4 — Shikhar Dhawan and Rohit Sharma (2018)Earlier, Finn Allen and Glenn Phillips led New Zealand to 225/8, the joint-highest total against India in T20Is and New Zealand's highest on home soil. Allen scored 45 off 24 balls, while Phillips remained unbeaten on 82 off 40 deliveries.With Jasprit Bumrah not part of the squad, India's bowlers struggled to contain the hosts. Despite some early swing, New Zealand's batters found ways to score freely, adding 67 runs in the final five overs.Axar Patel was India's most expensive bowler, conceding 51 runs in four overs. The innings also brought an unwanted record for India, as five bowlers conceded 40 or more runs in a T20I innings for the first time. It was the 13th such instance in men's T20Is overall.Bhuvneshwar Kumar conceded 49 runs in his four overs, Arshdeep Singh gave away 45, Mayank Yadav and Nitish Reddy conceded 40 each, while Axar finished with figures of 1/51.At the time of writing the story, India were 128/4 in 11 overs.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: One frame at a time! Story of Multan's Minhas brothers through their father's lens
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Kashif Minhas has captured thousands of photographs of cricketers over the years.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Kashif Minhas has captured thousands of photographs of cricketers over the years. He is also an avid birdwatcher who sometimes waits for hours to get that perfect shot. But when his sons are playing and he is busy behind the lens on the ground, the avid shutterbug finds it difficult to keep his nerves in check."I have thousands of photographs of international cricketers. When I am completely focused on a match, I become very attentive to every ball. Capturing a catch at the right moment is special. However, these days, when my sons are playing, I sometimes enjoy watching the cricket live more than photographing it," Kashif Minhas, who runs a car business in Multan for a living, tells TimesofIndia.com.Earlier this year, Kashif was caught on camera by the broadcasters after his elder son, Arafat Minhas, playing only his third ODI, got out against Australia at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. As Arafat was dismissed, Kashif, standing behind the boundary rope with his camera, could not hold back his emotions."I was clicking his photographs, and the moment he got out, I put my hand on the camera and lowered my head. The television cameras caught that reaction, and it went viral," he says.The world doesn't know about my third son, Abdullah Minhas. He is immensely talented as well. He is a left-handed top-order batter and a right-arm leg-break bowler. He has been selected at the Under-17 level and is working hard."They [the broadcasters] know I am his father, so they often keep a camera on me. I even asked the director not to focus on me because I did not want to be shown in front of everyone. People think I am an official photographer of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), which I am not. I freelance for a local newspaper, Daily Pakistan. But they told me that the visual had helped them garner a lot of views, so I thought, 'Chalo, kisi ka toh bhala ho raha' (At least someone is benefiting from it)," he adds.Kashif, however, was deeply hurt by the false stories that circulated after the visuals went viral."That story made me sad. We have been in the car business since 1980, and I have a large showroom in Multan. Some people portrayed the story as if we belonged to a poor family and I had started photographing my children because we had run out of money. That is not the case. Photography is just my hobby. I have a very good car business and import cars from Japan. I never needed money to fund my children's cricket," he says.Kashif's two sons, Arafat Minhas and Sameer Minhas, have shown the world what they are capable of. Arafat has played five ODIs and seven T20Is for Pakistan. The all-rounder has already taken two five-wicket hauls, one each against Australia and England, in his brief international career. Sameer Minhas has lit up age-group cricket, and one cannot forget his 172 off 113 balls against India in the 2025 U-19 Asia Cup final.Kashif says his third son is also getting ready."The world doesn't know about my third son, Abdullah Minhas. He is immensely talented as well. He is a left-handed top-order batter and a right-arm leg-break bowler. He has been selected at the Under-17 level and is working hard," says a proud father.Like many fathers in the subcontinent, Kashif, too, is a cricket tragic."I was also a cricketer. I represented my regional team in Multan. But my father asked me to quit cricket and focus on the family business. He told me to leave cricket or leave home. I left home for two or three days, but then my mother asked me to come back and give up cricket. Nothing is more important to me than my mother, so I quit," he recalls.But one fine day, while playing with a tape ball in their car porch, Kashif's eyes lit up when he saw Arafat and Sameer, then aged nine and seven, respectively, cutting, driving and pulling.When I saw my children playing, I immediately realised that they had something special in them. I decided that what had happened to me should not happen to them. I wanted them to have the opportunity to pursue cricket."The floor was wet, and their hand-eye coordination was amazing. When I saw my children playing, I immediately realised that they had something special in them. I decided that what had happened to me should not happen to them. I wanted them to have the opportunity to pursue cricket," he says."I took them to a local cricket academy, and when I saw how well they were playing against pace, I began to take their cricket more seriously. Arafat performed well in the PCB Under-13 tournament, then at the Under-16 and Under-19 levels. Sameer followed in his footsteps, and soon Abdullah will do the same. We kept trying and praying, and Allah blessed us," he adds.Kashif, who had to give up his own cricketing ambitions, acknowledges that cricket is a tough sport to succeed in and requires much more than time and money."It requires a lot of dedication. You have to make sacrifices. I was away with my children for their training when I heard the news of my father's death. After his demise, I had to spend a lot of time at the office. But whenever they played matches outside Multan, I would travel and sit at the ground from morning until evening," he recalls.As his sons progressed through age-group cricket, Kashif came up with the idea of taking up photography as a way to stay close to them. He started freelancing and soon found work with a local daily. As Arafat and Sameer began making waves with their performances, Kashif, too, became a familiar face on cricket grounds across Pakistan, camera in hand."It was an amazing moment for me," says Kashif, recalling Arafat's ODI debut against Australia in Rawalpindi."I never imagined that a day would come when my children would represent Pakistan in international cricket and I would be on the ground photographing them. It felt like a blessing, and I was very happy that day. He [Arafat] performed well in the last match [against England]," he further adds.Kashif has never been harsh on his sons regarding cricket. But he has one dream he hopes to fulfil through them: winning an ICC trophy."I was never harsh on them. When they were not performing well, I would tell them that it was not their day and that their time would come. I would encourage them to stay prepared for the next opportunity. I never wanted to put unnecessary pressure on them. But I will be even happier when my children win an ICC trophy for their country," he says.The Minhas family could have etched its name in the Guinness World Records, with members representing Pakistan at different age-group levels. But the PCB has declined a request from the over-50s team to participate in the International Masters Cricket World Cup, which is being hosted by India in January next year. Minhas Sr was a member of that squad. Pakistan won the previous edition of the tournament, held in Sri Lanka last year, but this time the board has informed the Pakistan Veterans Cricket Association that its team will not be permitted to travel to India and participate."It would have been great to represent Pakistan, but it's okay. I will get the chance later," he says.For Kashif Minhas, cricket has come full circle. He once had to abandon his own ambitions at his father's insistence, but he made sure his sons had the freedom to pursue theirs. Today, he watches them represent Pakistan, capturing their highs and lows through his lens while carrying the hopes of a father who knows what it means to let go of a dream. An ICC trophy would be the ultimate reward, but for Kashif, seeing his sons live the dream he once had to give up is already a journey worth cherishing.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sanju Samson special, Shreyas and Naman cameos help India pull off highest successful chase against New Zealand
articles.summary: Sanju Samson continued his consistent run in T20Is this year with a 67 off 33 balls as India pulled off their highest successful chase in T20 cricket,
articles.body: Sanju Samson continued his consistent run in T20Is this year with a 67 off 33 balls as India pulled off their highest successful chase in T20 cricket, beating New Zealand by four wickets in the first match of the five-game series in Christchurch on Thursday.Chasing 226, India got off to a flying start but lost their way in the middle overs before captain Shreyas Iyer and Naman Dhir helped them cross the finish line with two balls to spare. Shreyas scored 42, while Naman remained unbeaten on 42 off just 15 deliveries.Highest successful chases for India in T20Is226 vs NZ, Christchurch, 2026209 vs AUS, Visakhapatnam, 2023209 vs NZ, Raipur, 2026208 vs WI, Hyderabad, 2019207 vs SL, Mohali, 2009204 vs NZ, Auckland, 2020The second T20I will also be played at Hagley Oval on Saturday.India looked in control after racing to 94/1 in the powerplay, with Samson leading the charge. However, New Zealand spinners Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell brought the hosts back into the game, as India lost three wickets for seven runs. From 93 without loss, the visitors slipped to 122/4 in the 11th over.The long boundaries also played a part in India's middle-order collapse, with Ishan Kishan and Tilak Varma losing their wickets while attempting to clear the ropes.Samson, however, had already given India the platform they needed. He struck eight fours and four sixes in his 67, registering his eighth score of 50 or more in 26 innings this year. He targeted the straight boundary regularly, with his flick off Lockie Ferguson over long-on standing out.Abhishek Sharma supported Samson during their 93-run opening partnership, scoring 29 off 12 balls. He pulled Adam Milne for two consecutive sixes in the fourth over as India raced towards the target.With the chase in danger of slipping away, Shreyas took responsibility and kept India in contention. He also benefited from a reprieve when Finn Allen dropped a difficult catch in the 15th over. India needed 55 runs from the final 30 balls, with five wickets remaining.Naman joined Shreyas and struck timely boundaries to ease the pressure. Their contributions proved enough to take India over the line in a tense finish.Earlier, New Zealand posted 225/8 after being asked to bat, with Finn Allen scoring 45 off 24 balls and Glenn Phillips making an unbeaten 82 off 40. The total was New Zealand's highest on home soil and the joint-highest score against India in T20Is.Despite some early swing, the New Zealand openers found ways to score freely. Tim Seifert, who made 24 off 17 balls, attacked Bhuvneshwar Kumar after the Indian pacer bowled a decent first over. Seifert struck two fours and a six over long-on in Bhuvneshwar's next over, which cost 17 runs.Allen then attacked Arshdeep Singh, helping New Zealand build momentum in the powerplay. Mayank Yadav gave India a breakthrough when Seifert was caught behind off the final ball of the fifth over.Axar Patel, bowling the last over of the powerplay, conceded two sixes as Allen cleared long-off and Daryl Mitchell stepped out to hit over long-on. New Zealand reached 65/1 in the first six overs.Arshdeep later dismissed Mitchell, but India's bowlers struggled to contain the scoring. Bhuvneshwar conceded 49 runs without taking a wicket in four overs, while Axar gave away 51. Bevon Jacobs added 31 off 16 balls, including a first-ball six down the ground off Arshdeep, before Phillips finished the innings with a switch hit over cover.New Zealand scored 67 runs in the final five overs, setting India a target of 226. However, Samson's innings and the late contributions from Shreyas and Naman ensured the visitors began the series with a win.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
